research.title: The Personal Space Paradox
paragraphs: Researchers have discovered that people in love require two completely opposite things:
Personal space and constant attention.
The difficulty is that both are often required at exactly the same time.
One partner may say, “Leave me alone,” then become offended when the other actually leaves.
Dr. Bullshitzky has concluded that personal space is not a physical distance.
**It is a location that moves depending on someone's mood.**

research.title: The Unnecessary Touching Experiment
paragraphs: The Institute investigated why couples insist on touching each other when there is absolutely no practical reason to do so.
Common behaviors include poking, squeezing, stealing blankets, and placing freezing feet against another person's warm body.
The results were disturbing.
The more comfortable one partner becomes, the stronger the other partner's urge to interfere.
**Dr. Bullshitzky concluded that true love is the inability to see someone comfortable and leave them that way.**

research.title: The Last Bite Investigation
paragraphs: After observing couples sharing meals, researchers discovered that the phrase “I'm not hungry” has almost no scientific value.
A person may refuse an entire meal, then begin eating from their partner's plate.
When questioned, they insist they only wanted a bite.
Further testing revealed that a bite can involve up to half the available food.
**The Institute has concluded that food tastes significantly better when somebody else was planning to eat it.**

research.title: The Missing You Paradox
paragraphs: Researchers examined a strange pattern among couples who spend considerable time together.
After several hours of separation, both partners report missing each other.
However, within minutes of being reunited, one will begin deliberately annoying the other.
The Institute initially suspected a failure of memory.
Further testing suggests that **people do not necessarily miss their partner's behavior. They miss having access to it.**

research.title: The Blanket Ownership Dispute
paragraphs: A detailed investigation into sleeping couples has revealed that sharing a blanket does not result in equal blanket ownership.
One partner will gradually acquire most of the available material during the night.
The other wakes up freezing, confused, and reconsidering several life decisions.
Dr. Bullshitzky has established that **sleeping together is the only known arrangement in which two people enter bed equally and one wakes up with all the property.**
The Institute describes this as a remarkably peaceful form of organized theft.

research.title: The Dangerous Question Experiment
paragraphs: The Institute has identified a question that appears harmless but requires extraordinary caution:
“What are you thinking about?”
Researchers discovered that the person asking usually expects a deeply romantic answer.
Unfortunately, the other person may genuinely be wondering whether penguins have knees.
Dr. Bullshitzky concluded that **love requires accepting that the person who means everything to you may occasionally have absolutely nothing happening inside their head.**

research.title: The Vacation Famine Preparedness Syndrome
paragraphs: The Institute investigated why families pack enough food for a two-week emergency before leaving on a three-day vacation.
Researchers found that the destination may contain restaurants, supermarkets, and even functioning agriculture.
None of this reduces the amount of food packed.
**Dr. Bullshitzky concluded that humans do not fear starving on vacation. They fear paying for food they already have at home.**

research.title: The Buckwheat Superiority Complex
paragraphs: The Institute discovered that buckwheat possesses an unusual property.
Nobody can eat it without somebody else explaining how healthy it is.
The longer the nutritional lecture, the less enjoyable the meal becomes.
**Dr. Bullshitzky concluded that buckwheat is not primarily a food. It is a way of establishing moral superiority over someone eating potatoes.**
